Finite MEX insertion, periodic queues and window graph conventions

These models use explicit finite inputs. Their exact output identities do not assert that a canonical growing cascade can be supplied efficiently. No private state is identified merely because two carrier responses agree.

Dyadic matching and square-root windows

Here tokens have signs ±1\pm1±1 and positive integer dates; every finite date range contains finitely many tokens. A matching pairs opposite signs, each vertex at most once. An endpoint-ratio bound κ≥1\kappa\ge1κ≥1 means the larger date is at most κ\kappaκ times the smaller. Define WM(n)W_M(n)WM​(n) as the number of matching edges with one endpoint at date at most nnn, the other after nnn, and U(I)U(I)U(I) as the number of unmatched vertices dated in III.

Bucket each matched pair by k=⌊log⁡2min⁡(dates)⌋k=\lfloor\log_2\min(\text{dates})\rfloork=⌊log2​min(dates)⌋. Its endpoints are in [2k,2κ2k)[2^k,2\kappa2^k)[2k,2κ2k), so each bucket is finite. Sort its pairs by positive endpoint date; for a nonsingleton bucket add a cyclic edge from each positive endpoint to the next pair's negative endpoint. Parallel edges, if any, count with multiplicity. A singleton adds no edge. The completed graph has degree two at nonsingleton vertices, one at singleton endpoints, zero at unmatched vertices.

Each canonical matching, window, cut and increment supplier remains an explicit assumption.

Finally the unit-delay counterexample is self-contained: at date 2k2k2k put 2k2k2k positive tokens, at 2k+12k+12k+1 put 2k2k2k negative tokens, pairing equal local indexes. Its crossing inventory is 2k2k2k at even cuts and zero at odd cuts, O(n)O(n)O(n), but pointwise signed charge has absolute value 2k2k2k on both dates and is not o(n)o(n)o(n). This is an abstract event stream, not a canonical Chomp realization.
